source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain; only its historical definitions and examples are transcribed, not website editorial material.
transcription_source: Internet Archive volume 2 printed page scans and OCR, cross-checked against clean online Webster transcriptions; original OCR is retained unchanged.
selection_method: Selected the final four exact KJV-used S headwords in alphabetical order from the unreviewed high/medium OCR queue. This closes that targeted S queue, not the full Webster review backlog.
review_method: Visually checked every sense against the printed page scans and used clean online transcriptions only as secondary aids. Corrected OCR substitutions, scan breaks, column interleaving, page headers, punctuation, and numbering; retained historical examples, usage labels, and author citations. Expanded parts of speech and normalized whitespace for display. Source spans are one-based lines in the hash-verified OCR file.
review_scope: All definitions and examples: eight STRAIN transitive senses, two intransitive senses, and nine noun senses; the exact SUFFICED participle entry; sixteen SUPPORT transitive senses and seven noun senses; and three SUPREME adjective senses.

entries.review_note: Scan n676 confirms all eight transitive, two intransitive, and nine noun senses. The three-column OCR misplaced the transitive heading and first five senses inside the preceding STRAIGHTEN record, then interleaved senses 6-8 with the intransitive and noun entries; the deliberately broad source span covers every column fragment. Corrected damaged etymology, numbering, quotations, citations, usage labels, and omitted transitive material; excluded STRAINABLE and following entries.

Scan n697 confirms the exact two-line participle entry and pronunciation. Replaced the base record that had swallowed SUFFICIENCY, SUFFICIENT, and SUFFICIENTLY; those neighboring entries are excluded.

Scans n705-n706 confirm the etymology, sixteen transitive senses, seven noun senses, and the Dryden citation. Corrected the inserted SUP page headers, split words, OCR substitutions, damaged numbering, quotations, and punctuation. The printed noun's first unnumbered sense is normalized as sense 1 for consistent display; excluded SUPPORTABLE and following entries.

Scan n707 confirms all three adjective senses, the government examples, the statement that God only is supreme ruler and judge, and the final usage warning. Corrected replacement marks, damaged numbering, and OCR substitutions; excluded SUPREMELY and following entries.
